events.title: Not Just a Kid: An Exploration of Childhood in the United States Through Puppets
events.description: The ALab in the Department of Anthropology invites you to the opening reception of the exhibition by Angela Clark, “Not Just a Kid: An Exploration of Childhood in the United States Through Puppets” on October 9 (Friday), 12:30pm at Schleman 300. Lunch will be served at the opening. The exhibit will be open on weekdays from noon-2PM, until October 23rd. About the exhibit: The hegemonic thought about childhood in the United States is that children are not whole persons as they are yet to become the idealized form of adult. Hegemonic notions of time dictate that children are yet to be considered “worthy” as they are expected to mold themselves into their culture’s expectations, while not yet being seen as a valid community member. This exhibit critiques the damaging notion that children are simply “human becomings” by exploring their unique relationship to hierarchical paradigms. Children are often overlooked in conversations about systemic injustice, so working within The ALab’s mission to decolonize research, this exhibit utilizes puppets as an approachable and flexible artform to explore childhood through a decolonial lens. Artist Bio: Angela Clark (she/her), is a third year Purdue undergraduate student. She is an intern with The ALab, studying Anthropology and Development and Family Science, and currently exploring Western colonial attitudes towards childhood, childism, and children as a marginalized group in the United States. She is a puppet maker and uses puppets as a medium for multimodal research. Her puppets have been shown in community theater productions as well as educational spaces as a tool of artistic and academic expression. If you are interested in showing the exhibit to your students outside the above-mentioned open hours, please feel free to email Angela Clark at clar1026@purdue.edu to arrange a visit.

events.title: Executive Forum with Heath Billingsley, Vice President, Supply Chain Operations NA for Syngenta
events.description: The Executive Forum is open to the public, as seating permits, and provides opportunities for the exchange of ideas and discussion of topics and issues facing business and management. Heath Billingsley grew up in southern Illinois working in his family’s agricultural retail business, where he developed an early appreciation for the critical role supply chains play in agriculture. After earning a degree in Mechanical Engineering from University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign and an MBA from Tulane University, he built a global career spanning agriculture, manufacturing, and supply chain leadership. During his 17 years at Monsanto, Heath held a variety of leadership roles across the Crop Protection and Seeds businesses. A highlight of that time was building a greenfield production facility in Brazil, an experience that triggered his passion for leading teams in a global business context. Since joining Syngenta in 2012, Heath has held senior leadership positions across Europe, Africa, the Middle East, Latin America, and Asia. He currently leads supply chain operations for Syngenta’s North America Crop Protection business, with end-to-end accountability for balancing customer service, cost, and working capital across a complex supply network. Heath serves on the MBA Advisory Board of the Joseph M. Bryan School of Business and Economics at University of North Carolina Greensboro, where he works with students and faculty to connect academic concepts with real-world business challenges and enjoys sharing lessons from his global leadership experience in supply chain operations and business transformation. He also serves on the Board of Directors of United Way of Greater Greensboro, where he contributes his experience in strategy, operations, and organizational leadership to support the organization's mission and strengthen its impact in the community. Outside of work, he enjoys classic cars, cooking, travel, and spending time with his wife and two children in Greensboro, NC.

events.title: Lunch & Learn Series: Growing Up Vietnamese American in Little Saigon﻿
events.description: AAARCC Lunch & Learn Series An Immigrant Family Narrative: Growing Up Vietnamese American in Little Saigon﻿ Thursday, October 29 | 12:00 PM - 1:00 PM AAARCC (915 5th St) Session Description: Vietnamese American experiences are often understood through narratives of war, refugee displacement, and resettlement. Yet, these narratives tell only part of the story and fail to capture resilience and community. Drawing from her experiences growing up as a Vietnamese American woman in Orange County, California and her reflections on Suburban Refugees: Class and Resistance in Little Saigon, Phoebe Pham explores the complex histories of Vietnamese American communities beyond the conventional refugee narrative. Integrating personal experiences with psychological perspectives on ethnic identity and belonging, this presentation considers how subsequent generations inherit, navigate, and reinterpret stories that have shaped their communities. Attendees are invited to reflect on the histories embedded in their own communities and the stories they hope to preserve. Speaker Bio: Phoebe Pham is a second-generation Vietnamese American female doctoral student in Counseling Psychology at Purdue University. She received dual bachelor’s degrees in Psychological Science and Social Ecology from the University of California, Irvine. Reflecting on her lived experiences growing up in Little Saigon, she continues to explore how cultural narratives shape overall well-being. Her research and clinical interests include Asian American mental health, familial dynamics, and ethnic identity. As an aspiring family and play therapist, she hopes to return to her community in the near future to provide mental health services for Vietnamese Americans. ﻿About the Lunch & Learn Series: The AAARCC hosts a Lunch and Learn guest speaker series each semester on select Thursdays from 12pm-1pm at the AAARCC (915 5th St.) or a campus-specific location (listed for each session). events.title: 2026 SUPPLY CHAIN CONSULTING LECTURE SERIES
events.description: PURDUE STUDENTS ARE INVITED Students across Purdue majors and programs are warmly invited to attend any or all sessions. Join us to learn directly from industry professionals, ask questions, explore career paths, and connect classroom ideas with real-world supply chain and consulting practice. ABOUT THE SERIES The 2026 Supply Chain Consulting Lecture Series connects Purdue students with experienced supply chain executives, consultants, alumni, and industry professionals to explore how organizations solve complex supply chain and operations challenges in practice. The series is an integral part of SCOM 469 — Supply Chain and Operations Analytics Consulting, a 3-credit experiential learning course that transforms the classroom into a professional consulting environment. Student teams apply supply chain theory, data analytics, AI-enabled tools, and structured consulting methods to real-world business and industry challenges. THE THREE-PILLAR EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING MODEL Consulting & Industry Study Projects — Students learn by solving real business and industry problems through corporate-sponsored consulting engagements and advisor-guided industry studies.Mentoring Program — Experienced alumni and industry professionals coach student teams on problem solving, analytics, project management, executive storytelling, and professional development. Jeffrey R. Powers, retired IBM executive and Purdue alumnus, chairs the Industry Advisory Board.Industry Lecture Series — Practitioners bring current challenges, emerging technologies, leadership lessons, and real-world decision making directly into the classroom. SCOM 469 builds on Purdue’s university–industry partnerships and experiential projects with organizations including Wabash, Rolls-Royce, Corteva, Taste, and other corporate and industry partners. For Fall 2026, students will work through two experiential project pathways: the corporate project Taste Omnichannel Dining Service Optimization and the industry study Enhancing Pharmaceutical Supply-Chain Resilience. WHY ATTEND? Learn from experienced professionals — See how practitioners approach ambiguous, high-impact supply chain problems.Understand professional practice — Explore consulting, leadership, sourcing, planning, program management, and digital transformation in action.Connect analytics and AI to execution — See how data, analytics, and AI shape consulting strategy and day-to-day supply chain decisions.Connect classroom frameworks to real decisions — Examine constraints, cross-functional trade-offs, and the realities of implementation.Build your professional network — Meet Purdue alumni and experienced industry professionals while exploring supply chain career paths.All Purdue students are welcome. You do not need to be enrolled in SCOM 469 to participate. Attend the sessions that match your interests, come prepared to ask questions and share perspectives, and use the series as an opportunity to learn and build professional connections. FALL 2026 LECTURE SCHEDULE SEPTEMBER 3 — Consulting 101 Isaac Tipton — CEO, Prowire USA The opening session introduces the foundations of consulting and structured problem solving. Drawing on professional experience, the speakers will discuss how consultants approach ambiguous business problems, work with clients and teams, communicate insights, and translate analysis into actionable recommendations. SEPTEMBER 17 — Program Management in Supply Chain: From Plan to Execution Michelle Kozlowski — Senior Program Manager, Amazon Catherine “Cathy” Nash — Sales & Operations Execution Planner, Constellation Brands Strong strategies create value only when organizations can execute them. This session focuses on program management, planning, coordination, accountability, and execution—examining how supply chain professionals move from plans and priorities to operational results across people, processes, and functions. OCTOBER 1 — Trade-Off Management + Cross-Functional Procurement & Sourcing Decisions Amanda Tronchin — Finance & Strategy Consultant, Pinnacle Strategy Group Eduardo Da Silva-Witzke — Aftermarket Sourcing Analyst, Cummins Inc. Supply chain and procurement decisions frequently require balancing competing objectives across cost, service, risk, quality, capacity, and strategic priorities. This session explores how professionals structure trade-offs, collaborate across functions, and translate financial, operational, and strategic considerations into sourcing and procurement decisions. OCTOBER 15 — Leadership, Influence & the Human Side of Supply Chain Consulting Kriti Gupta — Director of Operations, Amazon Nilo Cedeno-Guadamud — Global Category Manager, Wabash Analytics alone rarely produces organizational change. This session explores the human side of supply chain leadership and consulting—including stakeholder influence, relationship building, communication, team leadership, negotiation, and the ability to move organizations from insight to action. OCTOBER 29 — AI in Supply Chain: From Consulting Strategy to Everyday Execution Vishal Madisetti — Associate, Emerging Platforms, KPMG US Brookelle Mathieson — Life Sciences Supply Chain Management Consultant, Accenture Possible contributor: Khushi Karmokar — Procurement Analyst, ThoughtSpot AI is changing both how consultants solve problems and how supply chain professionals perform everyday work. This session explores practical applications of AI, analytics, automation, and emerging technologies—from consulting strategy and transformation initiatives to operational decision support, procurement, and day-to-day execution. NOVEMBER 12 — Planning, Constraints & Supply Chain Systems Thinking Kyle Harshbarger — Supply Chain Engineer, Marathon Petroleum Lauren Heiss — Senior Technology Consultant, EY The final session brings together planning, constraints, technology, and systems thinking. The speakers will connect MRP/ERP concepts, bottlenecks, lessons from The Goal, and real-world planning challenges to the broader question of how supply chains operate as interconnected systems. The session will also explore supply chain career paths and how the strategic role of the supply chain function varies across industries. CONNECTING INDUSTRY AND THE CLASSROOM The Industry Lecture Series is not designed as a collection of stand-alone guest presentations. Each session is integrated with students’ consulting and industry-study work. Student teams are encouraged to bring questions from their projects into the classroom, apply lessons from speakers to their analyses, and reflect on how different professionals approach similar challenges across industries. Student ambassadors will also work directly with speakers before selected sessions to help prepare and contextualize the lectures, providing another opportunity to develop professional communication, stakeholder-management, and networking skills. Theory → Evidence → Insight → Recommendation → Impact HOSTED BY Zhan Pang Professor of Supply Chain and Operations Management Instructor, SCOM 469 — Supply Chain and Operations Analytics Consulting Purdue University REGISTER FOR SESSION UPDATES https://purdue.ca1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_2fB3x8h9fODi52S Questions? events.title: Executive Forum with Vivek Chakrabortty, Chief Executive Officer for The Kavi Group LLC
events.description: The Executive Forum is open to the public, as seating permits, and provides opportunities for the exchange of ideas and discussion of topics and issues facing business and management. Vivek was born in Mumbai, India, in a Brahmin Hindu and Catholic household and grew up in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, a Muslim country. One grandfather was an Indian Freedom Fighter, and the other was in the British Navy. From a very young age, my parents instilled an empathetic, diverse way of thinking in Vivek and his brother. His love for travel and desire to know people with different backgrounds and life stories is rooted in his own diversity. You could say he has been a risk taker and entrepreneur his whole life. He grew up in the rigorous and structured CBSE Indian school system where you had to choose between science, commerce, or arts at the age of 16. He craved freedom and knew that a path in America would enable him to be whomever he wanted to be. He negotiated with his dad to attend high school and college in the US, and moved when he was just 16. His life forever changed. It was only by chance that he started to work in operations resilience before two major US events happened: 9/11 and Hurricane Katrina. As a business continuity and crisis management consultant, he learned that businesses must be one step ahead of the threats faced by their clients whether they are natural disasters, civic unrest, terrorism, active shooters, cyber-security breaches, technology failures, or catastrophic accidents. He was the emergency preparedness advisor to the Louisiana Recovery Authority in the aftermath of hurricanes Katrina and Rita and led the California Healthcare Surge Planning which was the first of its kind in the U.S. in terms of scale and scope. The teams he led on these two projects were awarded the Chairman’s Award, PwC’s highest recognition for outstanding client service. In the past 25 years, he has worked in the American South, Northeast, Midwest, Pacific Northwest, California, and Mid-Atlantic. His work has taken him to Europe, Australia, and Asia. These experiences as well as his understanding of culture and people prepared him to be an entrepreneur. In 2014, his wife Kathy and Vivek invested their life savings to start the Kavi Group, a management consulting firm that provides business continuity and crisis management advisory services. Today, Kavi Group is a 7-figure company with Fortune 100 companies as their clients. Kavi has helped our clients navigate the COVID19 pandemic, supply chain risks and disruptions, geo-political conflicts, climate-change associated threats, and adjust to the new normal of risk management.

events.description: AAARCC Book Series Screening Precarity: Hindi Cinema and Neoliberal Crisis in Twenty-First Century India Refreshments provided. RSVP and reading the book prior to the events are not required to participate. If you need accommodation to participate in this event, please email aaarcc@purdue.edu. The Book Talk with Author is co-sponsored by Purdue Graduate Student Government. ﻿ Book Discussion Thursday, November 5, 2PM-3PM AAARCC (915 5th St) Learn about the history and theory of "precarity" from Chapter 1, including examples of how Bollywood films mediate the discussions of precarious public spheres in India. Free books provided for first 5 individuals who RSVP and attend the book discussion! aaarcc.short.gy/screenrsvp​ This book is open access for Boilermakers and can be downloaded for free from: aaarcc.short.gy/precarity Book Talk with Author Thursday, November 12, 12-1 PM AAARCC (915 5th St) and virtual Join Dr. Anwer for lunch and reflection about how her book examines a filmic rendition of precarity, and how Bollywood is "not just a site of representation, but as an economic-cultural vector in its own right." Cannot join in-person? Livestream available through Microsoft Teams: aaarcc.short.gy/screenonline​ About Book & Authors Megha Anwer is a Clinical Associate Professor in the Department of English and Assistant Vice Provost for Research & Scholar Development at John Martinson Honors College. Dr. Anwer's research centers on perspectives and theories from urban studies, critical race studies, feminist studies, postcolonial studies and violence studies in a global and transnational context. Anupama Arora is a Professor of English and Communication at the University of Massachusetts Dartmouth. This book explores the role that Hindi films play in how precarity is mediated by film and what that mediation reveals about both contemporary India and the social life of the movies. It examines 19 Bollywood films that constitute India’s precarious public sphere, characterized by a pervasive and profound sense of professional-personal insecurity experienced by the vast majority. Screening Precarity: Hindi Cinema and Neoliberal Crisis in Twenty-First Century India is an intervention in the politics of representation, particularly of how marginal identities are shaped, scripted and screened when neoliberalism and authoritarianism enmesh. It is also a cultural analysis of how the biggest film industry in the world is embedded in global media networks and marshals state power and star power, national histories and transnational fantasies, structural impossibilities and individual agency. ﻿Flyer: https://aaarcc.short.gy/screenflyer

events.title: Unlocking the Presidential Puzzle(s) with Mara Faccio
events.description: The Purdue University Research Center in Economics invites you to our November economic policy luncheon. Please register to join us for: Unlocking the Presidential Puzzle(s) with Mara Faccio 11:30 a.m.-12:30 p.m. Eastern Wednesday, November 11, 2026 Rawls Hall, 3rd Floor Commons 100 S. Grant Street Purdue’s West Lafayette campus Since 1927, the U.S. stock market has done substantially better under Democratic presidents than under Republicans, with the difference in annual stock market returns between the two parties averaging around 10% per year. This well-documented pattern has been dubbed the "presidential puzzle." Annual GDP growth shows a similar partisan gap. Faccio confirms this pattern using recent data. Before 1927, however, she finds that the "puzzle" reverses. Using data going back as far as 1791, she shows that annual stock market returns were almost 6% higher per year under Republican (or conservative) presidents. Annual GDP growth was 1.7% higher. Having examined competing explanations, Faccio concludes that the two opposing "puzzles" share one common source: investor risk aversion at election time. Whichever party won the election when risk aversion was high enjoyed higher subsequent returns. Mara Faccio is the Daniels School’s Tom and Patty Hefner Chair in Finance. Her primary research interests are in international finance and corporate finance. She is one of the most highly cited finance scholars. The PURCE faculty affiliate was among Stanford University and Elsevier’s top 2% of most influential scientists in the world for 2025. Space is limited for PURCE luncheons, and registration is required. Please register by noon on Friday, November 6. We look forward to seeing you in Rawls Hall for a catered lunch, networking, and a Q&A with Faccio following her talk. Parking is available in the nearby Grant Street Parking Garage. Reach out to us with any questions at purce@purdue.edu and (765) 494-3782. Learn more about our research center at business.purdue.edu/centers/purce.
